routes.html_budget_kib_note: 40 to match every other documentation page, and this is an alignment rather than a raise. This route had been running on the 35 KiB DEFAULT — the budget for marketing pages that carry no document — while being a documentation page that embeds a body like its siblings under /docs/, all of which get 40. Nobody chose 35 for it; it inherited it. Two things were fixed before this line was written, so the number is not buying cover for waste: DesignRuntimeBoot was shipping the THREADS body on this route, 7.59 KiB gzip of a document the page does not render and never declared (its own markdown twin is /docs/overview.md), and that is now the overview body it actually points at. The page sits at 35.27 KiB after both.

documentation.html_budget_kib_note: 40 is the ceiling for every documentation page; html_budget_kib_by_id tunes the ones that legitimately carry more, the same way the top-level routes above do. RAISED from 36 on 2026-08-07, when v0.19.9 could not publish: every page embeds the whole content corpus (24 doc bodies plus every tagged release), so ONE new release and ONE new page put four pages over at once while getting-started sat 0.2 KiB under. These numbers buy time; they do not fix anything. RAISED AGAIN for work-loops (42 -> 44 on 2026-08-10, then 44 -> 48 on 2026-08-11 when P7 AC1 added the first-integration loop — required content, not bloat, and the lane caught it at its own commit because web-quality now declares skill/**; the FOURTH raise is the argument for the filed repair, since 54% of this page is a payload unrelated to its text), and the third raise is the argument for the repair rather than against it: commit a09db83e added sixteen lines to skill/a2ahub/loops.md and the page crossed again. Worse than the raise was the delay — web-quality did not declare skill/** as a lane input, so the commit that caused it selected no web gate and went green; the Makefile now declares it, and the next one reddens at its own commit. On a documentation page that payload is 54% of the weight — work-loops is 41 KiB gzip with it and 16 KiB without — and the real repair is in docs/backlog.md.
documentation.html_budget_kib_note_2026_08_12: The work-loops override is GONE, and it was retired by the repair rather than by another raise. P13 split skill/a2ahub/loops.md (64 KB, thirteen jobs) into a routing root plus seven loop pages, and reference/data-exchange.md into three: work-loops went 52.60 -> 36.07 KiB gzip and data-exchange 40.52 -> 35.74, both under the 40 default, with no budget touched. Four raises had been spent buying time for this. Two things the split MEASURED that the note above got wrong, and they change where the next pressure comes from. First, the payload is not 'the whole content corpus' per page: docBodies is route-scoped, so it is the page's OWN body, which is why a page's weight tracks its own source and why splitting worked at all. What IS shared is compactDocs, a bounded 96-token entry per document. Second, and the consequence: adding TEXT is local, adding PAGES is not — the nine new pages cost every docs page ~2.2 KiB with no edit to it, so troubleshooting went 36.72 -> 38.87 and docs.html 31.79 -> 33.94 while nobody touched either. Those two, not work-loops, are now the binding constraint: ~1.1 KiB of margin each, and roughly five more pages would red docs.html without anyone editing it. The filed repair in docs/backlog.md is still the answer; what changed is that it is now about the shared index, not about the bodies.
